supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40:22, WS-DREYES-01 logged a network logon for paul.becker; shortly afterward, PowerShell ran on that workstation as paul.becker under the same logon ID.
The PowerShell command invoked \\FILE-COP-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1, matching the organization's stated IT patching practice. It then launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update package.
PowerShell made a proxy connection with a 38,800,205-byte response shortly after it started; the available Zeek record supports the transfer volume but does not identify its URL or contents.
UserAssist registry writes at 13:30:56 and 13:42:23 contain ROT13-encoded path text corresponding to powershell.exe. These records do not establish the command line or what that activity did.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy log collection was unavailable from 13:20 to 14:00 UTC, so proxy request details for the PowerShell connection cannot be reviewed; a Zeek connection record is available for it (T134-00129).
The UserAssist records provide path text but not command-line arguments or process details (T134-00068, T134-00151).
claims_not_established: The available evidence does not show the contents or integrity of Patch-Workstations.ps1 or establish what it did beyond the observed command and child process (T134-00125, T134-00131).
The available evidence does not establish whether the UserAssist PowerShell entries represent separate launches related to the alert, or what commands they might have run (T134-00068, T134-00151).
The destination and contents of the large PowerShell-associated proxy transfer are not established by the available connection record (T134-00129).
unrelated_findings: Google Drive File Stream started under dan.reyes; the inventory does not list it as approved cloud storage. This is a separate review item and does not determine the alerted PowerShell activity (T134-00261, T134-00262).

FILE-COP-01 made an inbound connection to WS-DREYES-01 on RPC endpoint-mapper port 135. The records do not establish its purpose; review separately, without treating it as evidence about the alerted PowerShell activity (T134-00277, T134-00279, T134-00280, T134-00281).
